**Observation Log:**

- [FACT] The user has been doing Hatha yoga for about 6 weeks.
- [PREFERENCE] The user enjoys Hatha yoga and is looking to mix it up with other classes.
- [EVENT] The user is looking for new yoga classes to try out.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant recommended several classes focused on flexibility: Hatha Yoga, Yin Yoga, Vinyasa Flow with a focus on forward bends, and Restorative Yoga.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant recommended several classes focused on balance: Vinyasa Flow with a focus on standing balances, Power Yoga, Iyengar Yoga, and Bikram Yoga.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant recommended classes that combine flexibility and balance: Anusara-Inspired Yoga, Kundalini Yoga, and Sivananda Yoga.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant advised the user to listen to their body and consult with a healthcare professional or yoga therapist before starting a new exercise routine.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided tips to improve Downward-Facing Dog, including proper alignment, working on flexibility, strengthening the upper body, engaging core and legs, using breath, modifying and adjusting, and practicing regularly.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant suggested a morning routine to help the user wake up early for yoga classes, including setting a consistent wake-up time, gradually adjusting wake-up time, creating a bedtime routine, preparing the night before, using a smart alarm, getting morning sunlight, finding a morning motivator, making a plan for the morning, being kind to oneself, and using positive self-talk.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided an example of a morning routine: 6:00 AM - Wake up, stretch, and drink a glass of water; 6:15 AM - Quick breakfast and morning routine; 6:30 AM - Get dressed and pack yoga gear; 6:45 AM - Head out the door to class.
- [PREFERENCE] The user is considering doing a yoga teacher training program in the future.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant explained that a yoga teacher training program typically involves a minimum of 200 hours of training, covering asana practice, yoga philosophy, anatomy, teaching methodology, and more.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant mentioned that programs may focus on specific styles of yoga, such as Hatha, Vinyasa, Ashtanga, Iyengar, Kundalini, or Restorative Yoga.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided preparation tips for yoga teacher training, including establishing a consistent practice, studying yoga philosophy, developing an understanding of anatomy, reading yoga-related books, assisting or observing classes, developing communication skills, preparing physically and mentally, researching programs, and setting clear goals.
